## Findings
- claim-1: For \(Q=J_{2,4}/A_+J_{2,4}\), quotient free ranks in degrees \(4,\ldots,24\) are \[ (1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0), \] i.e. \(1,1,2,1,1\) in degrees \(4,5,6,7,8\) and \(0\) in degrees \(9,\ldots,24\); every torsion-factor list is empty. [artifact baf9447fe15327ded6640cbb3b0b3c7b43b62cdb3fb6fa1afcb78fe218ca5d97]
- claim-2: Using the accepted interval presentation (supported only in degrees \(4,\ldots,24\)) and accepted identification of the complete \(A_+J_{2,4}\) Pieri-row lattice, the preceding Smith data give \[ J_{2,4}/A_+J_{2,4}\cong \mathbb Z^{1+1+2+1+1}\cong\mathbb Z^6. \]
- claim-3: The supplied source summary states that Theorem 5.4 provides two generating sets for \(J_v\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), each of cardinality \(\binom{a+b}{a}\). [source-6@L14-L42|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-4: For \(i=j=p=c=2\), \(a=b=2\), so each accepted generating family has \(\binom42=6\) elements. Since each maps to a surjection \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow J_{2,4}/A_+J_{2,4}\cong\mathbb Z^6\), accepted indexed-family Nakayama implies that both \[ \{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\} \quad\text{and}\quad \{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\} \] map to \(\mathbb Z\)-bases of the quotient. Hence neither has a proper subfamily generating \(J_{2,4}\).
- claim-5: The requested target is established: both listed families are minimal generating sets of \(J_{2,4}\). No broader minimality claim is concluded.
## Strategy
From artifact `baf9447fe15327ded6640cbb3b0b3c7b43b62cdb3fb6fa1afcb78fe218ca5d97`, the quotient ranks in degrees \(4,\ldots,24\) are
\[
1,1,2,1,1,0,\ldots,0,
\]
and all torsion-factor lists are empty. The interval presentation has degrees only from \(4=|(2,2)|\) through \(24=|(4^6)|\), so no degrees outside this range occur. Thus
\[
J_{2,4}/A_+J_{2,4}\cong
\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z^2\oplus\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z
\cong\mathbb Z^6.
\]

For \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,2,4)\),
\[
a=\min(p,c)=2,\qquad b=\min(i,j)=2,
\]
so each accepted generating family has \(\binom42=6\) elements. Each family therefore yields a surjection \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow J_{2,4}/A_+J_{2,4}\cong\mathbb Z^6\). By the accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion, its images are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis; hence neither family has a proper generating subfamily.

## Gaps
No gap remains relative to the accepted interval presentation, complete Pieri-row identification, computation artifact, generation result, and indexed-family Nakayama criterion. The computation evidence is internal project evidence, not an external source-backed theorem.

## Next
The requested \(c=4\) target is established: both displayed six-element families are minimal generating sets of \(J_{2,4}\). No broader minimality claim is made.
